## Findings

1. **F1 — Root lifecycle documentation falsely calls states terminal.** [README.md](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/README.md:118) labels `Done` and `Rejected` terminal and its diagram ends at `Done`; current update/reject handlers do not enforce a closed source-to-target state graph. Remediate by removing the terminal/no-return claim and describing the actual target-state guards.

2. **F2 — Type-label prose says every issue has exactly one type.** [docs/reference/labels.md](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/docs/reference/labels.md:132), [docs/examples/sdd/config.toml](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/docs/examples/sdd/config.toml:51), and [docs/examples/research/config.toml](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/docs/examples/research/config.toml:60) say “Exactly one per issue,” while the namespace uniqueness rule enforces at most one and type presence depends on configuration/rules. Remediate these descriptions to say “at most one,” explaining that a default or validation rule may require one.

3. **F3 — Dependency readiness is described incorrectly.** [docs/reference/labels.md](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/docs/reference/labels.md:53) says a dependency blocks work only until it is `Ready`; dependencies instead block until they reach `Done` or `Rejected`. Remediate the example to use terminal dependency resolution.

4. **F4 — Claim staleness is presented as configurable runtime behavior.** [docs/reference/claim.md](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/docs/reference/claim.md:255) and its configuration example describe a configured stale threshold, but claim handling currently uses a hardcoded one-hour stale threshold. Remediate by documenting the fixed threshold and marking the configuration field compatibility/display-only until runtime support exists.

5. **F5 — Stale indefinite leases are falsely said to be evicted automatically.** [docs/how-to/multi-agent-coordination.md](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/docs/how-to/multi-agent-coordination.md:137), [docs/how-to/multi-agent-coordination.md](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/docs/how-to/multi-agent-coordination.md:308), and [docs/concepts/guarantees.md](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/docs/concepts/guarantees.md:556) claim stale leases expire or are evicted by later acquisition. Automatic eviction applies only to finite TTL leases; stale indefinite leases remain until heartbeat, release, or `force-evict`. Remediate the lease-recovery guidance accordingly.

6. **F6 — Storage layout invents per-agent heartbeat files.** [docs/concepts/guarantees.md](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/docs/concepts/guarantees.md:366) describes `.git/jit/heartbeat/` as containing one file per agent. Heartbeats append to `claims.jsonl` and update the derived claims index; the directory is initialized but no per-agent liveness files are written. Remediate the layout description.

7. **F7 — Claim operations are falsely said to perform temporary-file recovery.** [docs/concepts/guarantees.md](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/docs/concepts/guarantees.md:445) says `jit claim` operations remove orphaned temporary files. Recovery is performed by `jit recover`, not ordinary claim commands. Remediate the guidance to direct users to `jit recover`.

8. **F8 — Scope documentation overstates ordinary issue claiming as atomic.** [docs/concepts/scope.md](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/docs/concepts/scope.md:187) says “Atomic claiming prevents conflicts.” `issue claim` and `claim-next` do not provide exclusive candidate selection; only `jit claim acquire` serializes advisory lease acquisition. Remediate with that distinction.

9. **F9 — Overview overstates event-log coverage.** [docs/concepts/overview.md](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/docs/concepts/overview.md:118) says events log “all changes.” The guaranteed invariant is logging issue state changes, not every repository mutation. Remediate to state the lifecycle guarantee and describe other event recording as selected operations.

10. **F10 — Troubleshooting falsely says `jit claim list` rebuilds the claims index.** [docs/how-to/troubleshooting.md](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/docs/how-to/troubleshooting.md:441) and [docs/how-to/troubleshooting.md](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/docs/how-to/troubleshooting.md:458) claim listing rebuilds or creates the index. A missing index is loaded in memory without being rebuilt; `jit recover` performs the repair. Remediate both recovery sequences to use `jit recover`.

Total findings: 10
